newsitem.title: UK: UK house prices rise 0.5 pct in February - Halifax.
newsitem.headline: UK house prices rise 0.5 pct in February - Halifax.

text.p: British house prices rose a seasonally adjusted 0.5 percent in February having fallen 0.7 percent the month before, the Halifax Building Society said on Thursday.
"The latest figure confirms our view that last month's downturn was simply a one-off adjustment for the larger-than-expected monthly rises at the end of 1996," a Halifax statement said.
It said the three-month on three-month rate of house price inflation -- 1.7 percent -- suggested the housing market continues to rise at a moderate pace.

Prices paid by first-time buyers leaped by 2.1 percent in February, reversing January's 2.0 percent fall. The annual rate of inflation for first-time buyers is now five percent, below the 5.7 percent rate seen the month before, but only because prices rose faster over the same period last year.
Prices of new houses are rising 0.8 percent every three months but continue to oscillate. In February alone they were up 5.8 percent year-on-year.
The Halifax forecasts annual house price inflation of seven percent in the fourth quarter of 1997.
